title: ChatGPT-4o Will Be Great for Certain Math, Certain Thinking, and Certain Kids
author: Dan Meyer
summary: Dan Meyer offers a skeptical read of OpenAI's GPT-4o demo videos, in which the model guides users through solving a linear equation and finding a sine ratio using multimodal camera input. While acknowledging the technology is impressive, Meyer argues tech and business leaders are asking none of the serious questions: what kind of math, what kind of thinking, and what kind of learner does this actually help? He contends the demos showcase 'calculation' -- important but not central to mathematics, analogous to chopping onions for a dinner party -- while GPT-4o's step-by-step guidance style risks training students on small ideas rather than the bigger conceptual ideas mathematics actually requires. He also questions the assumed universal appeal of AI tutors, citing a 2018 Khan Academy study in which only 11% of students used the software at its recommended weekly dosage, and argues that an 'infinitely patient' AI tutor is actually an ineffective one, because effective teachers proactively pursue disengaged students rather than passively waiting to be asked for help.
points: Meyer's central framing device: calculation is to mathematics what chopping onions is to hosting a dinner party -- 'important, but it is not central' -- and both GPT-4o demos showcase calculation rather than the fuller range of mathematical thinking.
He flags that GPT-4o's step-by-step guiding questions risk breaking big ideas into memorisable small steps students can master 'without understanding the big idea even a little.'

Citing a 2018 Khan Academy study, he notes only 11% of students used the software at its recommended weekly dosage even under ideal study conditions, evidence against assuming universal student enthusiasm for AI tutoring.

His sharpest line reframes the 'infinitely patient tutor' framing as a bug, not a feature: effective teachers proactively pursue disengaged students rather than waiting passively to be asked for help.
quotes: I can say with absolute certainty that GPT-4o will only help certain learners this certain thoughts about certain kinds of math. This is true of every new tool or medium.
But calculation is to mathematics what chopping onions is to hosting a dinner party. It is important, but it is not central. It is not a prerequisite for other kinds of work.

This question focuses the student on small ideas. It breaks a big idea—the equivalence of these ratios across similar triangles—into smaller ideas, ideas which a student can memorize and master without understanding the big idea even a little.
In a large 2018 study of thousands of students, Khan Academy reported that only 11% of participating students used its software for the recommended dosage of 30 minutes per week.
Many people describe generative AI as an infinitely patient tutor. They don't understand that this makes generative AI an ineffective tutor.
